contributions.statement: Do not compare retrieval, exploration or harness configurations using one LLM judge's verdicts gathered on different dates, even with a pinned model snapshot: re-judging the identical 300 inputs eleven weeks later agreed with the earlier verdicts at kappa 0.14 (GPT-5.4) and about 0 (GPT-4.1, +41 pp leniency) against a same-day test-retest kappa of 0.76, so judge all compared arms in one session on paired items and re-anchor the judge on a small human-labelled set.
contributions.evidence: §5.3 Table 3 same-judge controls on 300 paired tuples (binomial p<1e-44 against a stationary judge); snapshots pinned to gpt-5.4-2026-03-05 and gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 (§4). Caveats: binary faithfulness task, both judges from one vendor, no human labels, so which date's verdicts were right is unknown.

contributions.statement: When scoring a retrieval or exploration agent's trace or QA answers, compute citation precision over the IDs the answer actually cites, not over the context set it retrieved; a graph walk with context precision 0.12-0.23 cited at 0.48-0.65, and scoring the context set flips it from best to worst.
contributions.evidence: §5.2 C2a, Table 2, consistent across two embedders and two corpora. Caveats: only GraphRAG's context precision is tabulated, and the gap is partly built in by its 15-item context cap against vanilla's top-5.
relative_to: ALCE answer-level citation precision/recall (Gao et al. 2023)

contributions.statement: Do not rely on RAG, dense or graph-walk, to assemble trace chains of three or more links: citation F1 stayed at or below 0.254 for every pipeline on 3+-hop requirement queries, while 1-2-hop queries reached 0.69-0.76 with plain dense retrieval; when explicit trace links exist, traverse them deterministically and use the model only to explain.
contributions.evidence: §5.1 Table 1 (296 queries x 3 seeds x 2 embedders, Holm-Wilcoxon with effect-size threshold). Caveats: synthetic DO-178C-style corpus generated by the answering model's family, requirement-to-requirement links rather than code, and the deterministic-traversal alternative is implied but not tested.

contributions.statement: Do not default to an agentic retrieve-critique loop for short (1-2-link) trace lookups; with the same generator and embedder it scored 0.19-0.30 citation F1 below a single dense top-k call.
contributions.evidence: §5.1 Table 1 under both embedders. No mechanism, cost or latency reported; the loop has only a search tool and a 3-iteration cap, so it may be under-tuned.

contributions.statement: Compare a query router with the best single pipeline, not with a weak rule-based router; here the learned hop router (overall F1 0.559/0.569) only tied fixed GraphRAG (0.551/0.571).
contributions.evidence: Table 4 against Table 2 overall F1; the paper reports gap closure from the rule-based router instead.

reason: Two evaluation practices survive at moderate strength. The first is that pinned LLM judges drift to near-chance self-agreement over eleven weeks; the second is to score citations at the answer, not the retrieved set. A hop-dependence boundary for RAG-assembled trace chains also survives. All transfer only indirectly, because the corpus is a synthetic requirement graph with no code.
